==Problem==
A store increased the original price of a shirt by a certain percent and then lowered the new price by the same amount. Given that the resulting price was <imath>84\%</imath> of the original price, by what percent was the price increased and decreased<imath>?</imath>

<imath>\textbf{(A) }16\qquad\textbf{(B) }20\qquad\textbf{(C) }28\qquad\textbf{(D) }36\qquad\textbf{(E) }40</imath>

==Solution 1==
Suppose the fraction of discount is <imath>x</imath>. That means <imath>(1-x)(1+x)=0.84</imath>; so, <imath>1-x^{2}=0.84</imath>, and <imath>(x^{2})=0.16</imath>, procuring <imath>x=0.4</imath>. Therefore, the price was increased and decreased by <imath>40</imath>%, or <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(E)}\ 40}</imath>.

==Solution 1.1 == 

After the first increase by <imath>p</imath> percent, the shirt price became <imath>(1+p)</imath> times greater than the original. Upon the decrease in p percent on this price, the shirt price became <imath>(1-p)</imath> times less than <imath>(1+p)</imath>, or <imath>(1-p)(1+p)</imath>. We know that this price is <imath>84</imath> percent of the original, so <imath>(1-p)(1+p) = 0.84</imath>. 



From here, we can list the factors of <imath>0.84</imath> and see which are equidistant from <imath>1</imath>. We see that <imath>0.6</imath> and <imath>1.4</imath> are both <imath>0.4</imath> from <imath>1</imath>, so <imath>p = 0.4 = 40 \%</imath>, or choice <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(E)}\ 40}</imath>. 


~TaeKim

==Solution 2 (Time-Consuming)==
We can try out every option and see which one works. Wasting 30 mins of the 40 mins, by this method, we get <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(E)}\ 40}</imath>.

==Solution 3==
Let x be the discount. We can also work in reverse such as (<imath>84</imath>)<imath>(\frac{100}{100-x})</imath><imath>(\frac{100}{100+x})</imath> = <imath>100</imath>.

Thus, <imath>8400</imath> = <imath>(100+x)(100-x)</imath>. Solving for <imath>x</imath> gives us <imath>x = 40, -40</imath>. But <imath>x</imath> has to be positive. Thus, <imath>x</imath> = <imath>40</imath>.

==Solution 4 ~ using the answer choices (similar to Solution 2)==

Let our original cost be <imath>\$ 100.</imath> We are looking for a result of <imath>\$ 84,</imath> then. We try 16% and see it gets us higher than 84. We try 20% and see it gets us lower than 16 but still higher than 84. We know that the higher the percent, the less the value. We try 36, as we are not progressing much, and we are close! We try <imath>\boxed{40\%}</imath>, and we have the answer; it worked.
(OR: try (C) first to eliminate 2 answer choices)

==Solution 5 (A Variation of Solution 4)==

Let our original cost be <imath>\$ 100</imath>, so we are looking for a whole number of <imath>\$ 84</imath>. Also, we can see that (A), (C), and (D) give us answers with decimals while we know that (B) and (E) give us whole numbers. Therefore, we only need to try these two: (B) <imath>\$100</imath> increased by 20% = <imath>\$120</imath>, and <imath>\$120</imath> decreased by 20% = <imath>\$96</imath>, a whole number, and (E) <imath>\$100</imath> increased by 40% = <imath>\$140</imath>, and <imath>\$140</imath> decreased by 40% = <imath>\$84</imath>, a whole number.

Thus, <imath>40</imath>% or <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(E)}\ 40}</imath> is the answer.

~ SaxStreak

==Solution 6 (using factors)==

First find the prime factors of 84. These are 2,2,3 and 7. Using this, try the answers. For example, 100*1.2/1.2. This is equal to 120*0.8. If you find the factors of 12 and 8, you find that there is no seven and too many 2's. So <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 20}</imath> is out. Using the same method, you can find that 116*0.84 is out, as 84 already has all the factors of 84. 128*0.72 and 136*0.64 both don't have seven as a factor, so <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(A)}\ 16}</imath>, <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 28}</imath>, and <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 36}</imath> is out.  This leaves 140*0.6, which has just the right amount of factors (2^2,3, and 7). Therefore, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(E)}\ 40}</imath>

~ParticlePhysics
